Which film is said in the conversation t.Blade Runner: Blade Runner asks what makes us human, not how we escape illusion. The film named is about a world that is a simulation.

Which Greek astrophysicist does she cite.Dimitri Nanopoulos: Nanopoulos is a well-known Greek physicist of string theory, but not the one Athena cites when teaching the Cave.
Which Greek astrophysicist does she cite.Stamatios Krimigis: Krimigis is a Greek space scientist known for NASA missions to the planets. He is not the one Athena cites here.
Which Greek astrophysicist does she cite.Christos Papadimitriou: Papadimitriou is a Greek computer scientist, not an astrophysicist. Athena cites someone who speaks of an ocean of energies.

What does the story of Helen show, in he.She was a goddess in disguise: Helen is Zeus's daughter in myth, but the story Athena tells is about a double: an image sent in Helen's place.
What does the story of Helen show, in he.She never existed: The story does not erase Helen. The real Helen stayed elsewhere while her image went to Troy.
What does the story of Helen show, in he.She returned to Sparta at once: No version Athena tells has Helen sail straight home. The point is that the Trojan War was fought over an image.

What is her criterion that the path is n.You still have desires: Desire is sacred in its motive, Athena says; having desires does not mean the path is unfinished. The test is about identity.
What is her criterion that the path is n.You still feel pain: Realisation does not end pain; Athena describes a calm steadiness through hard events too. The test is whether an 'awakened' identity remains.
What is her criterion that the path is n.You still live in a body: Awakening happens in the body, by dis-identifying from it. Living in a body is no sign that the path is unfinished.

Who is the one wonder-worker?.Governments: Governments are outer wonder-workers that build mass reality, and Athena does name them. But the one wonder-worker is inside us.
Who is the one wonder-worker?.Religions: Religions too can build shadows for the crowd, Athena says. But the true wonder-worker sits inside each of us.
Who is the one wonder-worker?.The media: The media are the obvious modern wonder-workers. Athena turns inward: the images are finally produced in our own minds.

What is the prisoners' defining mark?.Cowardice: Cowardice is a failing of the spirited part. The prisoners' trouble is a kind of not-knowing.
What is the prisoners' defining mark?.Greed: Greed is a symptom of the cave, not its mark. The prisoners' defining condition is about what they know.
What is the prisoners' defining mark?.Laziness: Laziness would mean they know there is more and will not move. In fact they take the cave for the whole of life.

Which gate out of the cave does she add.A traumatic shock: A shock is one of the host's three gates, not the one Athena adds. Athena's addition is about timing rather than a blow.
Which gate out of the cave does she add.A 'healthy depression': That is the host's second gate, in his own phrase. Athena adds a fourth, about the soul's timing.
Which gate out of the cave does she add.The soul's eros: Eros, a great nostalgia of the soul, is the host's third gate. Athena's addition is a different one, about timing.

The Horai are daughters of Zeus and whic.Hera: Hera is Zeus's wife and mother of Ares, but the Horai's mother is the goddess of divine order.
The Horai are daughters of Zeus and whic.Mnemosyne: Mnemosyne is the mother of the Muses by Zeus. The Horai have a different mother, the goddess of justice.
The Horai are daughters of Zeus and whic.Leto: Leto is the mother of Apollo and Artemis. The Horai are daughters of a different goddess, linked to justice.

Which epithet of Hermes does she connect.Argeiphontes: Argeiphontes, slayer of Argus, recalls a deed of Hermes, not his role between worlds. Athena connects the returning one with the god as guide.
Which epithet of Hermes does she connect.Trismegistus: Trismegistus, thrice-great, names the later Hermes of the Hermetic writings. Athena's link is to the older guide who leads souls between the worlds.
Which epithet of Hermes does she connect.Kyllenios: Kyllenios names Hermes after his birthplace, Mount Kyllene. Athena's epithet describes what he does: lead souls.

How does she define a conviction (πεποίθ.Knowledge proved by reason: Proved knowledge is the opposite of a conviction. A conviction is an opinion held tightly, with no proof needed.
How does she define a conviction (πεποίθ.A recollection of the soul: Recollection is the soul activating what it truly knows. A conviction is a view about sensible things, held with feeling, inside the cave.
How does she define a conviction (πεποίθ.A law of nature: A law of nature holds whether or not anyone believes it. A conviction exists only because someone is invested in it.

Which philosopher of science does she ci.Karl Popper: Popper is known for falsification: theories must be open to refutation. Athena cites another thinker on why scientific communities resist new paradigms.
Which philosopher of science does she ci.Paul Feyerabend: Feyerabend argued 'anything goes' in method. The account of paradigms and resistance to them comes from a different philosopher of science.
Which philosopher of science does she ci.Imre Lakatos: Lakatos wrote on research programmes, a response to the thinker Athena cites. The idea of resisted paradigm shifts is the original one.

Who proposes 'mind emptiness' in place o.Athena Potari: Not Athena: Athena agreed it was a nice observation, but the coinage came from the person interviewing Athena.
Who proposes 'mind emptiness' in place o.Plotinus: Plotinus would surely approve of an empty mind, but the phrase is modern wordplay on 'mindfulness', from someone in the conversation.
Who proposes 'mind emptiness' in place o.Jung: Jung is not part of this exchange. The play on 'mindfulness' came from the conversation's host.

After leaving the cave, what does the fr.The sun directly: The sun comes last, once the eyes have adjusted. Looking at it straight away would blind the freed one.
After leaving the cave, what does the fr.The fire inside the cave: The fire is inside the cave, behind the prisoners; it is left behind on the way out. Outside, the first lights are gentler.
After leaving the cave, what does the fr.The wonder-workers' faces: The wonder-workers are met inside, on the way out, not after leaving. Outside, the first things seen are lights in the night sky.

Which Neoplatonic term names enlightenme.ὑπέρβασις: Ὑπέρβασις, transcendence, is the first movement: leaving the cave. The term asked for names the second: staying in the One while back in the world.
Which Neoplatonic term names enlightenme.ἐπιστροφή: Ἐπιστροφή is the return upward, the soul turning back to its source. The term asked for is about remaining in, here below.
Which Neoplatonic term names enlightenme.πρόοδος: Πρόοδος is procession, the outflow from the One. The term asked for names the One remaining in everything.

Besides compassion, why must the freed o.To punish the wonder-workers: Athena gives no punitive motive. The return is part of the path itself, not a settling of scores.
Besides compassion, why must the freed o.To be honoured by the prisoners: Honour is the opposite of what awaits: Plato says the prisoners would mock, even kill, the one who returns.
Besides compassion, why must the freed o.Because the light outside fades: The light outside never fades. The reason is that the path is not complete without going back into becoming.

What does she finally say darkness is?.The opposite of the Good: Athena says there is no real opposite to the Good: all is the Good. Darkness is not a second power.
What does she finally say darkness is?.Evil: Athena does not make darkness a positive evil. It is the same light, dimmed so much that it seems its opposite.
What does she finally say darkness is?.The body: The body is the field of the soul's descent for Athena, but darkness here is a degree of light, not a thing.

What are her two closing practices?.Fasting and prayer: Fasting and prayer are religious disciplines. Athena's two practices come from the two halves of the word 'philosophy'.
What are her two closing practices?.Reading and memorising: Reading and memorising are study habits. Athena's closing practices are about watching the mind and loving all beings.
What are her two closing practices?.Breathwork and chanting: Breathwork and chanting are body and voice practices. Athena's two come straight from φιλο- and -σοφία.

Which Plotinian phrase crowns her ladder.γνῶθι σαυτόν, know thyself: Know thyself is where the ladder of false selves begins, Apollo's command. The summit is a phrase of Plotinus about unity.
Which Plotinian phrase crowns her ladder.πάντα ῥεῖ, all flows: All flows is the saying tied to Heraclitus. The ladder of false selves ends with Plotinus meeting himself.
Which Plotinian phrase crowns her ladder.μηδὲν ἄγαν, nothing too much: Nothing too much is a Delphic maxim of measure. The ladder ends on a Plotinian phrase about unity.

What does she read the name Glaucon to m.The owl's wisdom: The owl, γλαύξ, does share the root γλαυκ-, gleaming, which makes this close. But Athena reads Glaucon as a quality of the soul: its brightness.
What does she read the name Glaucon to m.The sea's depth: Γλαυκός is often used of the gleaming grey sea, which is why this tempts. But Athena takes the word's brightness, not depth, and applies it to the soul.
What does she read the name Glaucon to m.The fearless one: Nothing in γλαυκός means fearless. It is a word of gleaming light.

In 'The Light of Hellenism', what does s.The land of the Greek peninsula: Athena does not read ΕΛ as geography. The root names a light, not a peninsula.
In 'The Light of Hellenism', what does s.The shared Greek language: Language matters to Athena, but the essay reads ΕΛ as a light, not as a tongue.
In 'The Light of Hellenism', what does s.The rule of rational law: Rational law is not what Athena finds in ΕΛ. The essay builds Hellenism around Light.

To which Indian notion does she compare.Karma: Karma is the law of action and consequence. Athena compares Logos to the consciousness that pervades everything.
To which Indian notion does she compare.Dharma: Dharma is right order or duty. Athena's Logos is not a rule but consciousness itself, present in all things.
To which Indian notion does she compare.Maya: Maya is illusion, the veil. Athena's Logos is the opposite: the real consciousness behind every form.

In her reading of Orphic theology, what.The gods go to war with the Titans: The war with the Titans comes much later in the myths. Athena's point concerns the first moment: Eros filling the void.
In her reading of Orphic theology, what.Time begins to devour its children: Kronos swallowing his children is a later episode. At Eros' emergence, in Athena's reading, the void becomes light.
In her reading of Orphic theology, what.The earth separates from the sky: Athena does not read Eros' emergence as a separation of earth and sky. In Athena's reading of the Orphic theology Eros is the bringer of light.

What do the letter groups ΑΛ, ΕΛ, ΗΛ nam.Three Greek dialects: Dialects differ by region, not by meaning. Athena reads the three groups as levels of light, with ΗΛ the visible sun's.
What do the letter groups ΑΛ, ΕΛ, ΗΛ nam.Body, soul and mind: Body, soul and mind are a triad of the person. Athena's three are tiers of light, from unmanifest to the visible sun.
What do the letter groups ΑΛ, ΕΛ, ΗΛ nam.Past, present and future: Athena's scheme is not about time. The three groups name three levels of light, ending in the sun's.

Who, for her, are the 'Hellenes' in the.Citizens of the Greek state: Citizenship is a legal status. Athena makes 'Hellene' a spiritual identity, open to all.
Who, for her, are the 'Hellenes' in the.Speakers of ancient Greek: Language alone does not make a Hellene in Athena's sense. The spiritual Hellene is defined by an inner realisation.
Who, for her, are the 'Hellenes' in the.Descendants of Hellen: Descent from the mythical Hellen is the ethnic meaning Athena moves beyond. The spiritual sense has nothing to do with ancestry.

Which teacher of Socrates does she cite.Aspasia: In Plato's Menexenus Socrates half-jokingly calls Aspasia his teacher of rhetoric. The path of love toward unchanging beauty comes from the priestess of the Symposium.
Which teacher of Socrates does she cite.Theano: Theano belongs to Pythagoras' circle at Croton, long before Socrates.
Which teacher of Socrates does she cite.Hypatia: Hypatia lived in Alexandria some eight centuries after Socrates, so she could not have taught him.

What does she say the word theoria comes.'Theatron': a place for watching plays: Θέατρον is a cousin from the same family of seeing, and Athena links theatre with beholding elsewhere. But here Athena reads θεωρία as seeing the divine itself.
What does she say the word theoria comes.'Thesis': a position to be argued: A thesis is something argued, which is what Athena says θεωρία is not. It is a direct vision.
What does she say the word theoria comes.'Theos' plus 'rhoe': the flow of the god: There is no flow in θεωρία. Athena hears a verb of seeing, joined to the divine.

Which Eastern path does she say experien.Confucian ritual ethics: Confucian ethics is about social ritual and roles. Athena compares Hellenic philosophy to paths of inner self-transformation.
Which Eastern path does she say experien.Zoroastrian dualism: Zoroastrian dualism sets good and evil against each other as two powers, the opposite of Athena's non-dual reading of the Greeks.
Which Eastern path does she say experien.Legalist statecraft: Legalism is a Chinese school of strict state control. It has nothing of the lived self-transformation Athena means.

Where was this essay first published bef.In the CHS Research Bulletin: The CHS Research Bulletin belongs to Harvard's Center for Hellenic Studies, but it was not where this essay first appeared.
Where was this essay first published bef.In Paradigm Explorer: Paradigm Explorer did not first publish this essay. It came out first in an online journal of philosophy as practice.
Where was this essay first published bef.In her Oxford thesis: This is a short essay, not part of a thesis. It first appeared online in 2021.

Whose question opens the Call?.Socrates: 'What is justice?': What is justice is the Republic's question. The Call opens with a question about who we are.
Whose question opens the Call?.Heraclitus: 'Can one step twice in the s: The river belongs to Heraclitus and flux. The Call opens with a question about human identity.
Whose question opens the Call?.Pythagoras: 'What is number?': Pythagoras is central to Athena, but the Call opens with a Neoplatonist's question about who we are.

Which earlier documents does the Call ex.The Universal Declaration of Human Right: Human rights and European degree reform are not what the Call extends. It builds on two documents challenging materialism in science.
Which earlier documents does the Call ex.The Club of Rome report and the Brundtla: The Club of Rome and Brundtland reports are about ecology and growth. The Call extends two post-materialist texts on science.
Which earlier documents does the Call ex.The Oxford Charter and the Harvard Core: Those are not the Call's starting points. It extends to the Humanities two recent texts arguing against materialism in science.

What does she call the situation of scho.The double bind: A double bind is a no-win demand. Athena's phrase describes scholars who live one way in private and another at work.
What does she call the situation of scho.The silent majority: The silent majority is a political phrase. Athena's term names a split within each scholar, between inner experience and public work.
What does she call the situation of scho.The academic closet: That is not Athena's phrase. Athena speaks of a life split in two, experiences kept apart from one's academic work.

Whose work on the brain's hemispheres do.Daniel Dennett: Dennett is a materialist philosopher of mind, close to the view the Call questions. Athena cites a psychiatrist who writes on the two hemispheres.
Whose work on the brain's hemispheres do.Antonio Damasio: Damasio is a neuroscientist of emotion and the body. The work Athena cites on the hemispheres is by someone else.
Whose work on the brain's hemispheres do.Oliver Sacks: Sacks wrote case histories of the brain. The hemispheres argument Athena cites comes from The Matter with Things.

According to the Call, what were the Hum.Training civil servants in rhetoric: Rhetoric for officials was one use of education, but not the purpose Athena names. The Call says the Humanities first tended the spirit.
According to the Call, what were the Hum.Preserving national languages: Languages are part of the Humanities, but preserving them is not their original aim in the Call. That aim was spiritual.
According to the Call, what were the Hum.Preparing students for scientific career: That reverses the Call's argument. The Humanities' first purpose was the inner life, not service to the sciences.

Whom does she credit with first using th.Socrates: Socrates walked the path, but Athena credits the word to someone earlier: the founder of philosophy as a spiritual path.
Whom does she credit with first using th.Thales: Thales is often called the first philosopher, but he is not credited with the word. Athena gives that credit to the sage of Samos.
